title: Classes for skill, attention, and connection.
intro: Learn in a supportive environment where technique, consent, and communication are taught together.

classes.title: Beginner Foundations
classes.description: Learn core rope handling, communication, simple ties, and safety practices in a supportive beginner-friendly setting.

classes.title: Rope For Connection
classes.description: Explore pacing, attention, negotiation, and presence through accessible exercises for partners and self-tying students.

classes.title: Decorative Floor Work
classes.description: A gentle introduction to elegant shapes, body-aware tension, and expressive ties without suspension.

bringText: Comfortable clothing that allows movement, water, a notebook if you like, and any rope you already own.
Loaner rope availability can be added here once class logistics are finalized.

details.title: Levels
details.text: Beginner classes can start from the first knots. More focused classes can list prerequisites such as basic rope handling or specific ties.

details.title: Partner or solo
details.text: Some classes work well for pairs, while others can include self-tying or solo practice. Add class-specific participation details here.

details.title: Group size
details.text: Smaller groups leave more room for personal attention, questions, pacing, and careful feedback.

detailImage.alt: Coiled rope arranged as a natural fiber detail
detailImage.label: Coiled rope detail

safetyText: Students are expected to participate with respect, sobriety, clear consent, and care for their own and their partner's limits. Suspension and advanced risk topics are not included unless explicitly listed for a class.

faqItems.question: Do I need experience?
faqItems.answer: No experience is needed for beginner classes. Each class description can note any prerequisites.

faqItems.question: Can I come without a partner?
faqItems.answer: Class formats can vary. Add details here about solo students, partner rotation, or partner-required classes.

faqItems.question: What kind of rope should I bring?
faqItems.answer: Students can bring rope they already own, or this section can list recommended rope types and loaner availability.
